scenes.title: Athena Hides the Walk through Scheria
scenes.card: Disguised as a girl carrying water, Athena guides the hidden Odysseus through the city and tells him to seek out Queen Arete.

subs.text: Book seven.
Phaeacia's Halls and Gardens.
Scene one.
Athena Hides the Walk through Scheria.
Go softly, stranger, and wait among my father's poplars until I am within.
Nausicaa enters the city wrapped in a divine mist.
You look lost, stranger.
Come, I will bring you to the house you seek, for it lies near my own father's.
These Phaeacians love oar and sail and do not warm to strangers, so walk quickly and question no one.
Go straight through the hall to the queen, Arete, whom the people honor like a god.
Win her heart, and you may yet see your home and your own high-roofed house.

scenes.card: Odysseus stands amazed before the king's palace, with its golden doors and an orchard that bears fruit all year.

subs.text: Scene two.
The Palace and the Gardens.
Walls of bronze, and doors of gold on silver posts —
a light lies on this house like the sun and moon together.
Fifty women within, some grinding the yellow grain, some at the looms —
their hands flicker like poplar leaves in wind.
Outside, an orchard and garden bear fruit through every season.
Odysseus crosses the threshold under mist and finds the royal feast in progress.

scenes.title: Supplication at Arete's Knees
scenes.card: Odysseus kneels before Queen Arete and begs for passage home; after a long silence, the king raises him and promises a ship.

subs.text: Scene three.
Supplication at Arete's Knees.
Athena's mist falls away only when Odysseus reaches Arete.
Arete, daughter of Rhexenor, after many trials I come to your knees, and to your king,
and to all these feasters —
may the gods give you long joy.
For me, ask only this:
grant me convoy to my own country, for I have suffered long, far from everyone I love.
Alcinous, this is not well, and it does not befit you:
a stranger sitting in the ashes of your hearth.
Raise him up, seat him on a silver-studded chair, and let the herald mix wine,
for Zeus himself walks with suppliants.
You honor me beyond my hope, great king.
May the gods repay this house.

scenes.world: An antique hall lit by a central hearth fire, smoke and dim firelight, staged like a silent costume drama.

captain.asks: Hold a frontal, frozen hall around the hearth while Odysseus kneels at Arete's knees and then sits in the ashes, until the old man speaks.
diagnosis: The supplication itself, the knees clasped, never appears: the central gesture of the scene is a smeared hand.
The hall changes every cut: Mélies cave, white staircase house, grand-hotel dining room with waiters, colour toy set.
Isolated good bodies (bust, turbaned elder, figure at the stone hearth) cannot be stitched into one room by a stranger.

scenes.title: Arete Recognizes Her Work
scenes.card: The queen recognizes the clothes he wears; Odysseus tells of his shipwreck without giving his name, and King Alcinous promises him passage.

subs.text: Scene four.
Arete Recognizes Her Work.
The hall empties;
only the king and queen remain.
And Arete's eye comes to rest on his cloak and tunic —
cloth her own hands wove with her women.
How you obtained them?
Hard to tell all my griefs, queen, for the gods have given me many.
Far off lies an island where the goddess Calypso held me seven years against my will,
and when at last I sailed, the sea broke my raft and threw me naked on your shore.
It was your daughter who found me, fed me, and gave me these clothes —
blame her for nothing, for I chose to walk behind alone, fearing men's idle talk.
One thing only my daughter missed, that she did not bring you straight to our doors —
yet your care does you credit, stranger.
Would to Zeus a man like you might stay, and be called my son, with house and wealth from my hand.
But no one holds you against your will:
tomorrow you shall have ship and oarsmen for your home, though it lie farther than the farthest island.

sign.operation: Insert of the cloak's pattern, then Arete's look from it to his face; the cloak framed beside her own maids' work.

scenes.world: The same firelit antique hall at night after the guests leave, empty benches, lamps burning low.

captain.asks: Insert the woven cloak, then let Arete's gaze travel from it to the stranger, demarking the cloth as her own work in the low-lit emptied hall.
diagnosis: The demark never closes: there is a cloth and there are hands, but no look from cloth to man, so the recognition is absent.
A 'Queen of Hearts' title card and a coloured cartoon flood every alternative column, proof the machine is matching words, not images.
Fire, sparks and storm sea give a consistent dark bw texture, but the story told is weather, not a court interrogation.

prologue: Following the princess's advice, Odysseus walks into the Phaeacian city, hidden by a mist Athena wraps around him. He must win over the king and queen without revealing who he is. These people could carry him home by ship.
